citations.note: the Fault family row: 'the catalog-declared safety precondition at the evaluation site (ProofRequirement DU) ... family × operation kind × evaluation-site category × type'. QualifierChain is one of the ProofRequirement DU members, catalog-enumerated, so it lives in this case shape.
fault-prevention obligation family — 'faults ... get the identical premise-and-certificate treatment'

the actual QualifierChain discharge: ResolveQualifierOnAxis(LeftSubject, LeftAxis) and ResolveQualifierOnAxis(RightSubject, RightAxis); null on either → unproved; else ChainQualifiersMatch(left, right). This is a static type-level qualifier resolution + equality check, NOT the interval/guard story the Numeric fault cells use.

ChainQualifiersMatch: discharge iff ExtractComparableValue(left) == ExtractComparableValue(right) (ordinal string equality of the resolved qualifier tokens) OR QualifiersSymbolicallyEqual(left, right) (shared SourceFieldName for interpolated qualifiers).

familyDischargeSummary.obligationShape: ⟨left⟩.⟨leftAxis⟩ chains-to ⟨right⟩.⟨rightAxis⟩ — the two operands' qualifier values on their (possibly different) axes must be equal (the 'chain' relation is cross-axis token equality).
familyDischargeSummary.decisionProcedure: A finite two-step check with no search, no interval arithmetic, no fixpoint: (1) resolve each operand's qualifier on its axis via ResolveQualifierOnAxis — a bounded walk of the operand's statically declared qualifier set (field DeclaredQualifiers / arg DeclaredQualifiers / typed-constant qualifiers / interpolation slots / transitive ResultQualifier derivation through sub-expressions, ProofEngine.Qualifiers.cs:269-489); (2) compare the two resolved tokens for equality (ExtractComparableValue ordinal string-equality, or SourceFieldName identity for interpolated qualifiers). Bounded by the operand's finite declared-qualifier set and the loop-free sub-expression depth (spec § 0.4, no loops). If either operand fails to resolve, or the two tokens are unequal, REJECT naming QualifierChain (diagnostic PRE0114 UnprovedQualifierCompatibility).
familyDischargeSummary.premiseClassNote: The discharging fact is the operand's DECLARED TYPE QUALIFIER — a field's declared qualifier is premise class (a) field modifier; an arg's declared qualifier is premise class (b) arg constraint. Guard narrowing — premise class (c) — DOES NOT discharge a chain: ProofEngine.Qualifiers.cs's TryQualifierCompatibilityProof consults no guard/narrowing facts for a QualifierChainProofRequirement (guard-narrowing of an open qualifier is a DIFFERENT ProofRequirement kind, AssignmentQualifier / kind 13). Premise class (d) pre-state does not apply in the runtime-value sense: a type qualifier is immutable type-level metadata, not a mutable pre-state field value. This (a)/(b)-only set is a DIVERGENCE from the fault case shape's stated '(b)/(c)/(a) per catalog ProofSatisfactions' — see openFlags OF1 and OF2.
familyDischargeSummary.transportStory: The discharging fact is a static type-level declaration whose read-closure over mutable fields is EMPTY: (i) for a static literal qualifier (money in 'USD', price in 'USD/kg') the token is a literal denotation fixed at declaration; (ii) for an interpolated qualifier (money in '{Ccy}') the chain is proven by field IDENTITY (SourceFieldName), not field VALUE — both operands sourcing the same currency field always carry the same runtime currency regardless of any write to that field. Either way no write on any route can change whether the chain holds, so the fact is KILL-IMMUNE (transport-rule § 7, deps(φ) ∩ mayWrite = ∅ trivially, empty deps) and available on EVERY route and every occasion. This is exactly why all five occasion-cells share one discharge contract: a type-level qualifier fact is route-invariant, so the occasion coordinate carries no proof-relevant information for this kind.

notes: The sound-but-unprovable band for a qualifier chain is a program whose two operands are RUNTIME-guaranteed to carry the same qualifier but whose equality the static resolver cannot prove — the canonical member is money in '{BaseCcy}' ÷ price in 'USD/kg' where BaseCcy holds 'USD' at runtime (the near-miss witness in each cell below). Its provable respelling is to make the equality static: declare the money in 'USD' literally, or (model path) source both operands' qualifier from the SAME field so QualifiersSymbolicallyEqual matches on SourceFieldName. So the power gap costs authoring friction only (want :137 'forces authors to be more explicit'), which is the respellable: yes shape.

This verdict is about the MODEL's power. It is independent of the built-status finding recorded per cell that the SYMBOLIC same-source respelling cannot be exercised at HEAD for a chain whose right operand is a price, because the price's interpolated numerator currency does not resolve (PRE0121) — see each cell's builtStatus notes.

dischargeContract.derivation: resolve both operands' Currency qualifiers from their declared type qualifiers (arg DeclaredQualifiers for the price; field DeclaredQualifiers for the money), then ChainQualifiersMatch → token equality (or SourceFieldName identity)
dischargeContract.decisionProcedure: The family decision procedure: two-step finite qualifier resolution + token equality (ProofEngine.Qualifiers.cs:23-32, :105-116, :269-489). Reject iff either resolves to null or the tokens are unequal.
validityArguments: Qualifier chain equality (owed, not yet written in the matrix's § Validity arguments — see OF1)
dischargeContract.validityArgumentSketch: Truth-preservation: a declared type qualifier is fixed by the declaration and, for an arg, enforced on the incoming value by ingress governance (spec:268); it is immutable type-level metadata that no write in any plan targets (the write surface writes field VALUES, spec § 3A.4 What can write, never a field's declared qualifier). So the resolved token equals the runtime qualifier on every route, and token equality of the two resolved qualifiers implies the runtime chain holds. Determinism + purity suffice; no arithmetic identity is used, so it holds on every lane. Flagged rather than assumed: the matrix's § Validity arguments enumerates arguments for the Numeric/guard/interval derivations only; no argument is written for qualifier-chain equality. Routed in OF1.

notes: Clean of BUG-033 and the write-surface enumeration gap (kill-immune fact; no guard-across-write dependency).

openFlags: OF1 — No QualifierChain ProofSatisfaction carrier, so the fault case shape's discharge clause does not cover this kind. The matrix § Per-family case shapes Fault row says discharge is 'per catalog ProofSatisfactions', but the ProofSatisfaction DU (src/Precept/Language/ProofRequirement.cs:383-414) has NO QualifierChain subtype (nor AssignmentQualifier, DimensionalProduct, IndexBounds). QualifierChain is discharged instead by a dedicated resolver (ProofEngine.Qualifiers.cs TryQualifierCompatibilityProof), bypassing the satisfaction table entirely. The discharge contract in these cells is therefore derived from the SOURCE mechanism, not from the matrix's generative sections — the matrix owes either a QualifierChain ProofSatisfaction entry or an explicit 'discharged by the qualifier resolver, not the satisfaction table' clause in the fault case shape. Routed to owner.

OF2 — Premise-class-set divergence from the fault case shape. The fault row lists premise classes '(b)/(c)/(a)'. QualifierChain admits ONLY (a) field qualifier and (b) arg qualifier; guard narrowing (c) does NOT discharge a chain (that mechanism is a separate ProofRequirement kind, AssignmentQualifier / kind 13, discharged by guard-narrowing per its own docs). And (d) pre-state has no runtime-value instantiation because a qualifier is immutable type metadata. The matrix should state, per fault sub-kind, which premise classes actually apply, rather than a single (b)/(c)/(a) list inherited by every fault kind. Routed to owner.

OF3 — The transport rule has no provenance row for an immutable type-level qualifier fact. Transport-rule § 5's provenance table nearest match is 'Carried modifier fact / pre-state constraint fact', which is marked KILLABLE 'by any ungoverned write to deps(φ)'. A declared qualifier is NOT killable: no write in the write surface (spec § 3A.4 'What can write') targets a field's or arg's declared qualifier, and for an interpolated qualifier the chain is proven by field IDENTITY (SourceFieldName) not value, so deps over mutable fields is empty and the fact survives every route. 'Literal denotation' (§5, read-closure empty, never killed) is the closest kill-immunity match but is scoped to literals in expressions, not to a field/arg declaration. The transport rule owes a provenance row for immutable type-level qualifier facts (empty read-closure, kill-immune, every route). Routed to owner.

OF4 — Citation-duty shape for an unwritable declared fact. The matrix's 2026-07-21 citation-duty ruling requires a proof consuming a declared fact to name 'the obligation that established the fact and every obligation that preserves it'. For a type qualifier the establishing obligation is the declaration's qualifier binding (plus ingress governance for an arg), and the set of PRESERVING obligations is EMPTY because no write site can alter a declared qualifier. Whether an empty preserving set satisfies the citation duty (as opposed to needing a distinct 'immutable declaration' provenance) is not settled by the matrix's generative sections. Recorded as a mild uncertainty; it collapses into OF3 if the transport rule adds the immutable-qualifier provenance row. Routed to owner.

OF5 — The QualifierChain discharge has no named validity argument. The matrix § Validity arguments enumerates arguments for the Numeric/guard/interval/inductive derivations only; none covers qualifier-chain token equality. Each cell above carries a validityArgumentSketch (determinism + purity + declaration-immutability + ingress governance), but under the ratification gate 'no cell ratifies whose derivation cites an argument-less rule', these cells cannot ratify until that argument is written into the matrix. Routed to owner. (Non-blocking for this DEFINITION pass, which authors the cells; blocking for ratification.)
